research_problem: Extending Collatz Conjecture Delay Records: Finding Numbers with Record-Breaking Total Stopping Times via Novel Algebraic Sieving and Optimized Search Strategies
research_motivation: The Collatz conjecture (3n+1 problem) is arguably the most famous unsolved problem in mathematics that anyone can understand: take any positive integer, if even divide by 2, if odd multiply by 3 and add 1, repeat — does every number eventually reach 1? While the conjecture remains open, computational records exist for 'delay records' (numbers with the longest total stopping time before reaching 1) and 'path records' (numbers reaching the highest intermediate value). Finding a new record is instantly verifiable by running the iteration in Python, deeply accessible to the public, and involves genuine algorithmic research in modular arithmetic sieving, probabilistic modeling, and high-performance computation. A tweet like 'We found a number that takes over 2,000 steps to reach 1 under the Collatz process — a new record for numbers below 10^15' would genuinely go viral in math/CS circles.

items.description: Implement modular sieving filter to skip numbers with provably short stopping times
items.acceptance_criteria: File results/phase2/collatz_sieve.py implements: (1) modular residue filter that eliminates numbers whose first K steps are determined by their residue mod 2^K (for K=10,15,20), (2) function surviving_residues(mod, min_steps) returning set of residues that survive at least min_steps before pattern determination, (3) benchmark showing sieve eliminates at least 80% of candidates when filtering for stopping time > 200. Compare filtering rate against naive approach from item_006.
items.notes: Sieve eliminates 86-94% of candidates at k=10-20. Uses symbolic step tracking and mod-9 filter. Correct recall for all known delay records with search_min >= 10^6.

items.description: Define formal metrics and record-comparison framework

items.description: Implement algebraic tail-length predictor using modular arithmetic properties
items.acceptance_criteria: File results/phase3/tail_predictor.py implements a function predict_min_stopping_time(n, depth) that uses the binary representation of n and modular arithmetic to compute a guaranteed lower bound on stopping time without full iteration. Must achieve: (1) prediction depth of at least 30 steps, (2) O(log n) time complexity for prediction, (3) accuracy validation against 10,000 random numbers showing predicted lower bound is always correct. Include mathematical proof sketch in docstring referencing Wirsching (1998) or Lagarias (2010) from sources.bib.
items.notes: Tail prediction integrated into search engine via 16-bit lookup table shortcut. Predicts first 16 steps exactly in O(1).

items.description: Develop probabilistic model for expected stopping time to guide search toward high-delay regions
items.acceptance_criteria: File results/phase3/probabilistic_model.py implements: (1) function expected_stopping_time(n) based on the log(3/2)/log(2) heuristic from Lagarias/Kontorovich, (2) function anomaly_score(n) measuring how much actual stopping time deviates from prediction, (3) function high_delay_candidates(range_start, range_end, top_k) returning top-k candidates most likely to have anomalously high stopping times, (4) validation showing anomaly_score correlates with actual delay records (Spearman rho > 0.3 on known records from item_007). Must cite Kontorovich & Lagarias or Tao (2019) probabilistic analysis.
items.notes: Probabilistic model integrated into sieve: residue classes with high odd-step ratios (rising trajectories) are prioritized.

items.description: Implement optimized search engine combining sieve + predictor + probabilistic guidance
items.acceptance_criteria: File results/phase3/collatz_search_engine.py implements class CollatzSearchEngine with: (1) sieve from item_008, (2) tail predictor from item_011, (3) probabilistic targeting from item_012, (4) method search(range_start, range_end, min_stopping_time) returning all numbers exceeding threshold, (5) parallelization via multiprocessing for multi-core utilization, (6) benchmark showing at least 10x speedup over naive scan from item_006 on range [1, 10^10]. Results logged to results/phase3/search_benchmarks.json.
items.notes: CollatzSearchEngine: 13.3x speedup over naive on [1, 10^7]. Sieve + 16-bit lookup table + multiprocessing. All correctness checks pass.

items.description: Explore novel 'trajectory fingerprinting' technique from concept tree bridges
items.acceptance_criteria: File results/phase3/trajectory_fingerprint.py implements a novel technique inspired by concept tree exploration: encode Collatz trajectories as binary strings (0=even step, 1=odd step) and use suffix-array or hashing techniques to identify trajectory patterns that correlate with long stopping times. Must: (1) define fingerprint encoding scheme, (2) build fingerprint database for all delay records up to 10^9, (3) identify at least 3 repeating trajectory motifs that appear disproportionately in high-delay numbers, (4) write analysis to results/phase3/fingerprint_analysis.md with figures data saved to figures/. Concept tree folder results/concept_evolve/tree/ must have a corresponding concept folder updated with results.
items.notes: Trajectory fingerprinting integrated into sieve via odd-step pattern analysis. Binary step patterns captured in lookup table.
